grand_champion.title: Cleat for stall chains
grand_champion.pitch: Trainees breaking real things plagues stall chains. The fix: filmed tasks become step-by-step SOPs with checkpoints, output supply counts, the expert approves and the system does the rest.
attacks: A-creativity-hawk: The training angle for stall chains is fresh and addresses a real pain point with SOP automation.
B-feasibility-hawk: Over-scoped: video analysis, supply counts, and approval system too complex for 8 days
C-platform-native: Limited validation on real-world implementation beyond basic image recognition
D-demo-hunter: Visual SOP generation from filmed tasks with expert approval creates instant payoff
E-work-realist: Vague SOP creation; no proof of expert approval workflow

board.title: Bellows Bench
board.pitch: The phone becomes the tool — the machine plate unlocks the exact manual page for jewelry workshops: piece tracking minutes after the work happens, auto-makes a 30-second recap the owner will repost.
attacks: A-creativity-hawk: Creative use of manual pages for jewelry workshops with auto-recap is unique but less ambitious.
B-feasibility-hawk: Voice-to-text for jewelry workshops is thin but feasible with real business value
C-platform-native: Niche application with limited scalability beyond jewelry workshops
D-demo-hunter: Jewelry piece tracking with auto-generated recap shows immediate value
E-work-realist: Manual page tracking unclear; no artifact specified

board.title: Lintel for maintenance teams
board.pitch: Work orders without the paperwork: the machine plate unlocks the exact manual page built for maintenance teams, ends in printed QR cards for the wall.
attacks: A-creativity-hawk: QR cards for maintenance teams is practical but feels like a slight variation on the theme.
B-feasibility-hawk: Similar to Bellows but less clear value proposition for maintenance teams
C-platform-native: Similar concept to Bellows Bench but with less creative application
D-demo-hunter: QR cards for maintenance manuals provide tangible demo moment
E-work-realist: 'Work orders without paperwork' lacks quantifiable time savings

board.title: Produce Quality Inspector
board.pitch: Automatically grade fruits/vegetables from photos for market standards
attacks: A-creativity-hawk: Produce grading is a solved problem with no creative twist on the concept.
B-feasibility-hawk: Image grading for produce is well-trodden territory with no clear differentiator
C-platform-native: Underutilizes Meta models, only basic image segmentation without advanced features
D-demo-hunter: Fruit grading lacks visual excitement and demo potential
E-work-realist: Common application; no named worker or defensible savings
